voci.titolo: Traders Grow Wary of Copper Bull Market With No Sign of Tariffs
voci.riassunto: Since Donald Trump came back into office, copper has surged on a seismic reshuffling of global inventories linked to the risk that he’ll impose tariffs on the metal. But as Trump nears the halfway mark on his second term, the market’s many bulls are growing wary that prices could crash if he doesn’t follow through.

voci.titolo: Bond Market’s Big Short Bet Gets Wakeup Call as AI Trade Wobbles
voci.riassunto: US Treasuries are showing tentative signs of reclaiming their traditional role as a haven — threatening to wrong-foot investors who are heavily positioned for this year’s bond slump to deepen.

voci.titolo: CPI Test Set to Make or Break New Zealand Dollar’s Losing Run
voci.riassunto: The New Zealand dollar has fallen for five straight quarters and if analysts are right, it may be on course to test a pandemic-era low.

voci.titolo: ‘Some people did everything right’: I lost my home in the Great Recession. I rent in my 50s. Why is that judged as failure?
These surprising stocks could be some of the biggest drivers of S&P 500 earnings growth
voci.riassunto: Boeing, Meta and EchoStar recorded steep charges and expenses a year ago, which are expected to make this latest quarter’s results look especially strong by comparison.

voci.titolo: U.S. budget deficit swells to almost $2 trillion for fiscal 2026, up 12% in a single year
voci.riassunto: The Treasury Department published the U.S. budget deficit for the 2026 fiscal year.

voci.titolo: Analysis: Why a $2 trillion deficit and 5% Treasury yields are becoming America's biggest economic challenge
voci.riassunto: Treasury yields above 5% are raising borrowing costs for households and the federal government, highlighting the challenge of financing $2 trillion deficits.

voci.titolo: Analysis: Everyone expects the Fed to hold rates in October. Kevin Warsh could surprise us all
voci.riassunto: Investors expect the Fed to pause rate hikes in October, but Kevin Warsh's rejection of traditional communications practices and continued concern about inflation leave the decision uncertain.

voci.titolo: Wholesale prices jumped 6.3% annually in September, biggest gain since 2022
voci.riassunto: September producer prices were expected to increase 0.6% month over month and 5.5% annually, according to the consensus estimate by Dow Jones.

voci.titolo: Economists: Hot PPI shows Fed's work is not done
voci.riassunto: 'We see real risks the Fed will deliver another rate hike in two weeks' time,' one Fedwatcher warns

voci.titolo: U.S. Treasury dismisses IMF debt warning and 'messy' forecasting
voci.riassunto: The exchange comes as U.S. debt exceeds $40 trillion and 10-year Treasury yields remain above 5%, intensifying scrutiny of the fiscal outlook.

voci.titolo: In charts: How one of the world's biggest economies got trapped by debt
voci.riassunto: France opens debate on its 2027 budget as high deficits, rising debt and student protests intensify pressure on lawmakers.

voci.titolo: China indicates rare earths will keep flowing to EU, regardless of U.S. trade deal expiration
voci.riassunto: European trade commissioner Maroš Sefčovič met with Chinese Commerce Minister Wang Wentao in Beijing last week.

voci.titolo: UK economy grew 0.1% in August, beating expectations
voci.riassunto: The U.K. is grappling with a cost-of-living crisis sparked by sticky inflation and surging energy costs.

voci.titolo: IMF sees milder global slowdown as AI boom offsets war hit — warns resilience is nearing limits
voci.riassunto: The IMF raised its 2026 global growth forecast to 3.1%, warning that resilience is tested by energy constraints and looming fiscal risks.

voci.titolo: How high inflation became a 'fact of life' in the U.S.
voci.riassunto: U.S. inflation has stayed elevated for years, raising concern at the Federal Reserve that consumers may come to expect stubbornly high prices.

voci.titolo: Consumer prices rose 3.7% annually in September as gas prices skyrocket
voci.riassunto: The consumer price index was expected to increase 0.6% in September on a monthly basis and 3.6% from a year ago, according to the Dow Jones consensus forecast.

voci.titolo: 'Godzilla El Niño' is wreaking havoc with Philippine central bank's inflation forecasts
voci.riassunto: The Philippine central bank is running policy scenarios for a severe El Niño on top of the oil shock, with inflation at a three-year high.
